title: Usage-curve-based reservation rebalancer and invoice adjustor
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers on Dedicated purchase reserved throughput (reservations) but actual usage curves vary intra-period. Current billing applies static reservation consumption windows and separate burst accounting which can create two problems: (1) conservative per-hour reservation allocation leads to customer-visible overages during short high-utilization spikes even when overall committed throughput covers usage, and (2) post-facto SLA credits are coarse-grained and difficult to reconcile with sub-hour rebalancing needs. This ticket proposes a usage-curve-based reservation rebalancer paired with an invoice adjustor workflow to reduce false overages and automate prorated SLA credits without opening manual disputes.
proposal_summary: Introduce a rolling reservation rebalancer that continuously prorates reserved throughput across the billing period using the observed usage curve; maintain a short-lived soft headroom buffer to absorb spikes; and generate a deterministic invoice adjustor that applies per-customer, per-period prorated reservation credits or micro-invoice adjustments when usage patterns indicate misalignment. The system will be deterministic and auditable: every adjustment is backed by an event stream and a human-readable rationale appended to the invoice metadata.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
1) Rebalancing window: We will use an exponential smoothing of per-hour usage with a configurable half-life to weigh recent activity more heavily. Tradeoff: smaller half-life reacts faster but may create oscillation; larger half-life is stable but slower to adapt. Initial default: 12 hours.
2) Soft headroom: Reserve a small % of committed capacity as temporary headroom (default 8%). This reduces false overages but increases potential platform exposure; to mitigate, headroom use is capped and amortized back into billing if unused.
3) Billing model: Apply a two-step accounting change — (A) real-time provisional adjustments that prevent immediate overage triggers and (B) consolidated invoice adjustor that posts final prorated credits at the end of billing period. This keeps runtime controls separate from ledger finalization.
4) Auditability: All adjustments are event-sourced and tagged with the algorithm version and parameters. Tradeoff: increased storage and complexity, but necessary for dispute resolution and compliance.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (Spike): 2w - Build simulation harness that replays historical dedicated pool traces; evaluate smoothing half-lives and headroom %; produce estimated reduction in overages and cost exposure. Phase 2 (Pilot): 3w - Implement rebalancer as a service that publishes provisional adjustment flags to tenant contexts and prevents immediate overage-based throttles when provisional headroom covers the spike. Expose feature toggle per-tenant. Phase 3 (Ledger integration): 3w - Implement invoice adjustor that consumes the rebalancer event stream and emits ledger neutralizing credits or micro-adjustments to invoices; include reconciliation and dispute endpoints. Phase 4 (Rollout): 2w - Pilot with small set of high-usage tenants, monitor chargebacks and dispute rate, then ramp.
Deliverables: simulation results, rebalancer service + feature flag, ledger plugin for invoice adjustor, customer-facing invoice metadata, rollout runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Simulations show >=60% reduction in false-overage events for pilot tenants using default smoothing and headroom
No more than 0.5% additional platform capacity exposure across pilot pools under stress testing
Rebalancer publishes deterministic events with algorithm version and parameters and events are retained for at least 90 days
Invoice adjustor produces human-readable invoice entries with rationale and is reconciled in nightly billing job without double-billing
Pilot tenants report <=1 billing disputes related to reservations during the pilot window
metrics_and_monitoring: Primary metrics: false_overage_rate, provisional_headroom_utilization, post_adjustment_net_revenue_delta, dispute_rate, latency_of_rebalancer_decision. Dashboards: billing-ops/usage-rebalancer, alerts for provisional_headroom_utilization>75% and post_adjustment_net_revenue_delta<-X% (configurable).
backwards_compatibility_and_migration: By default feature is opt-in per-tenant. Existing invoices remain unchanged unless tenant opts-in. For committed contracts with fixed SLO language, Platform will require account team sign-off before activation. Migration steps documented in rollout runbook. Ledger entries are additive credits (not rewrites) to preserve existing invoice immutability semantics.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: Customers may perceive credits as opaque. Mitigation: include explicit, line-item invoice entries with clickable explanation; provide a per-tenant simulation view in Console showing hypothetical impact before enabling.
Risk: headroom could be abused if many tenants use spikes in same pool. Mitigation: per-tenant caps, pool-wide guardrails and dynamic throttles.
Risk: legal/compliance concerns for retroactive adjustments. Mitigation: consult finance and legal; implement opt-in and add clear T&Cs for pilot customers.

notes_for_support_team: If a tenant reports unexpected crediting, support should: (1) capture tenant ID and billing period, (2) run the replay tool link in attachments to reproduce, (3) escalate to ENG-78201 with event IDs. Provide template response explaining line-item credit and pointer to Console preview.
estimated_cost_and_quota_impact: Runtime: small additional CPU/RAM for rebalancer service per pool; storage: +5GB/month for event retention per pool. Expected temporary cost exposure equal to headroom usage, tracked under billing-ops:expected_headroom_exposure metric.
